sentences.text: This animal belongs to the genus Nasutoceratops and is considered a basal member of the Centrosaurinae subfamily.
It features an unusually deep yet short snout and a nearly circular neck frill that is widest at its center.
Its brow horns can grow to 457 millimeters, the longest recorded for any centrosaurine, while low crescent-shaped epiossifications sit on the frill margins.
The holotype skull measures approximately 1.5 meters in length.

Sampson and colleagues described the genus and species in 2013 after finding the first specimens in the Kaiparowits Formation of the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument in Utah starting in 2006.
A subadult specimen was chosen as the holotype for Nasutoceratops titusi, a name honoring paleontologist Alan L. Titus for his work at the monument.

The holotype was collected with an articulated left forelimb, a fragmentary right forelimb, parts of the pectoral girdle, neck and back vertebrae, and three patches of skin impressions on the left forelimb.
Estimates suggest the animal reached a body length of 4.5 meters and weighed 1.5 tons.
The purpose of the deep front of the skull is unknown, though it may relate to chewing.
Researchers propose that the forward-oriented brow horns might have allowed the animal to interlock with opponents, similar to modern bovids.
Nasutoceratops lived in what is now North America during the Late Cretaceous Campanian stage, between 75.9 and 75.5 million years ago.
Argon-argon dating indicates the Kaiparowits Formation was deposited between 76.1 and 74.0 million years ago, during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
It is debated whether Nasutoceratops would have developed typical centrosaurine hooks and spikes if it had reached full maturity.
Researchers cautioned that more material, particularly parietal bones, is needed to determine the position of nasutoceratopsins near the base of Centrosaurinae.
According to this study, the existence of Nasutoceratops would support the hypothesis of faunal separation between the north and south of Laramidia.
